clues: This town lies in the south heart of Bolivia, set high in the hills. It is the world's next-highest capital, just below Quito.
It sits so high that its air stays cool all year long. That height gives the town its cool highland feel.
This town was the first capital of its land, long ago. It was a chief hub of the old Charcas court lands as well.
Its old core is one of the best-kept towns from Spanish rule in the west. UNESCO put the whole town on its World Heritage list.
By law this town is the true capital, and the land's top court sits here. Yet most state work moved long ago to La Paz.
